$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.check.common.docs. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-CONFIG-BLIND
arms.note: the width stops coming from the file's own hxformat.json, so a project declaring 60 gets this repository's 140 and its over-width comment lines are reported clean

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-CODE-BLIND
arms.note: the rule stops asking whether the COMMENT is what puts the line over, so a short marker riding a 174-column line of code is reported as a comment-width finding the formatter owns

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-TRAILING-WRAPPED
arms.find: refusal: i == 0 && headHasCode ? TRAILING : inFence ? FENCED : SourceComments.reflowRefusal(text)
arms.note: a comment trailing after code reads as own-line prose, so the rule offers a fix whose continuation would be a NEW own-line comment the writer then relocates

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-FENCE-BLIND
arms.note: the fence state is never consulted, so a line inside a ``` code sample reads as prose and the fix breaks the sample at spaces

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-PROTECTION-OFF
arms.note: the protection list goes, so a whole-body edit re-wraps every over-width line of the block including the ones no surviving finding asked for

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-CLOSER-UNSEEN
arms.find: reflow(source, unit, body, [w.body], metrics, unit.to - bodySpan.to)
arms.note: the probe stops handing the reflow the block closer, so a one-line doc block over by exactly its `*/` comes back unwrapped and is blamed on having no break point instead of being fixed

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-OPAQUE-OPEN
arms.note: the raw `#if` regions come back empty, so a comment whose bytes the model dropped is offered a fix no tree can corroborate

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-BARE-NUMBER
arms.find: return unit < 0 ? null : { at: at, to: unit, shape: 'a duration' };
arms.replace: return { at: at, to: digits, shape: 'a duration' };
arms.note: the unit stops being required, so every number in prose reads as a reading and a doc naming the code's own minimum or maximum is reported as one

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-ARROW-ANY
arms.find: return left < 0 || right < 0 ? null : { at: left, to: right, shape: 'a before-and-after pair' };
arms.replace: return { at: at, to: arrow, shape: 'a before-and-after pair' };
arms.note: digits on both sides stop being required, so a function type, a lambda and a map entry described in prose each read as a before-and-after pair

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-VERB-UNGATED
arms.find: if (lineHasDigit(source, from, to, at)) return { at: at, to: token, shape: 'a recording verb beside a number' };
arms.replace: return { at: at, to: token, shape: 'a recording verb beside a number' };
arms.note: the recording verb no longer needs a number beside it mid-clause, so prose saying what the code itself measures is reported as a reading of a tree

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-VERB-ANY-DIGIT
arms.note: a digit inside inline code beside the recording verb mid-clause makes it a record again, so a code sample the sentence quotes is reported as a reading

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-PERCENT-REMAINDER-BLIND
arms.note: the remainder guard inverts, so prose about operator precedence reads as a share and a share written as one stops being read at all

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-CLAUSE-BLIND
arms.note: every position reads as a clause opening, so the recording verb in the passive voice, as an adjective, or glued to a prefix is reported as a claim

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-REFERENCE-BLIND
arms.note: a marker inside a path or a URL, and one on a doc-tag line, stop being references, so a pointer at where the numbers live is reported as if it carried them

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-CENSUS-NOUN-ANY
arms.note: every word after a count reads as a census noun, so a contract's own bound on a dimension (lines, members) is reported as a census of a tree

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-CENSUS-FLOOR
arms.note: a single-digit count and a version number read as census-sized, so a fixture's own size and a language version before a noun are reported as readings

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-CENSUS-CODESPAN
arms.replace: if (insideCodeSpan(source, from, at) && at < from) return null;
arms.note: a count fenced as inline code stops being quoted data, so a tool's output quoted in prose is reported as a census

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-SHORT-ID-TYPE-BLIND
arms.note: a short id written as code stops naming a type, so a type parameter in backticks or after a colon is reported as a slice or backlog id

arms.name: M-DOC-CLAIM-CENSUS-BOUND-BLIND
arms.note: a bound, a standard's or a year's number and a count glued to the token before it all read as a census, so a doc stating the code's own limit or a version is reported as a reading

arms.name: M-DOC-LENGTH-CONFIG-BLIND
arms.note: the project's declared maximum stops being read, so a project asking for a shorter contract gets this rule's default and its own long blocks are reported clean

arms.name: M-DOC-LENGTH-ANY-COMMENT
arms.note: a line-comment run and a plain block banner read as doc blocks, so prose that belongs to the statements it stands over is reported as an over-long contract

arms.name: M-GATE-NOOP-DOC
arms.note: doc-coverage asking for no docs is reported as running

arms.name: M-FRAGMENTED-DOC-MERGES-ORPHAN
arms.note: two blocks that each open a doc are merged, so an orphan doc of a moved member becomes part of the next declaration's doc
